summary: Allegany State Park's 60-foot Aermotor tower on South Mountain, built 1926, closed 1970, restored and reopened 2006; open on set days, and sources disagree on the stairs.

facts.design: 60-foot standard LS40 Aermotor steel lookout tower
facts.agency: New York State Office of Parks, Recreation, and Historic Preservation

access.note: Sources disagree. The Southern Tier listing says the tower is fenced and off limits except on limited dates. The DEC says the stairs can be climbed but the top platform is closed. FFLA newsletters list set open days (Saturdays in 2021; June 20, 22 and 24, 2026, all past as of 2026-10-09). Check with Allegany State Park before visiting.

visit.trail_note: A 2020 FFLA newsletter says the trails around the summit are a mountain-biking area, with no horse trails near the summit.

events.note: Built by the Allegany State Park Commission on South Mountain as a 60-foot LS40 Aermotor tower.
By the end of 1928 the park had five towers in operation; Summit was one of the three main towers.
The Bureau of Forest Fire Control took over operation of the tower.
Fire lookout operations ended at the end of the 1970 season because of increased aerial detection.
The Fire Tower Restoration Committee, part of the Allegany State Park Historical Society, was formed.
Restoration completed; the tower reopened with a ceremony on October 14, 2006.
An FFLA newsletter says the tower is officially open on Saturdays from 11:00 to 1:30.
An FFLA newsletter lists the tower as open on June 20, 22 and 24, from 11am to 1pm.

corrections.why: The record's 20 m comes from an OpenStreetMap height tag. The Wikipedia article gives a 60-foot-tall (18 m) tower, and the Southern Tier listing gives a 60-foot tower.

notes_for_editor: The record's height_m 20.0 is proposed for correction to 18.0 (60 feet). Access is the main open question: the Southern Tier listing (fenced, limited dates) and the DEC listing (stairs climbable, top closed) disagree, and the 2021 and 2026 newsletters show set open days. A human should confirm current access with Allegany State Park before the page goes public. Staffing as a fire lookout ended in 1970; no later staffing is recorded. A 2019 FFLA newsletter (Friends of Allegany State Park climbing days) could not be fetched from the guessed URL (404), so it is not cited. A search snippet mentioned a 66-foot height from a park article; that page was not read and is not used. No fires are named in the sources read. No photos added.
